edit.description: `isCjsContextLoadFailure` reads the await shapes the page now names, and `CjsContextLoadError`'s doc states the set it matches
the CJS-context describe's case per named shape, driven through the real loader

summary: A CJS-context host whose chain graph carries a top-level await relays esbuild's raw TransformError, past the refusal that exists so no consumer reads a loader stack

per.section: tsx decides a module's interop shape from the nearest `package.json` `type`

acceptance: every CJS-context load failure the page names — the import-outside-module parse, the `?namespace=` resolution, and the top-level-await refusal in either position — reaches `CjsContextLoadError` with the `"type": "module"` fix, while a transform failure that is not about the cjs output format still surfaces as itself
tests: a CJS-context host whose chain carries a top-level await throws CjsContextLoadError naming the fix
a CJS-context host whose chain imports a module carrying a top-level await throws CjsContextLoadError naming the fix
pins: a chain whose transform fails on a syntax error surfaces that error rather than the CJS-context refusal
notes: Measured this tick through `loadChainModule` on tsx 4.21: a top-level await in the chain or in a module it imports throws esbuild's `TransformError` — `not supported with the "cjs" output format` — matched by neither arm of `isCjsContextLoadFailure` (`src/chainLoad.ts:219`); the same graph under `"type": "module"` loads to shape validation, so the standing fix line is right. `ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE` did not reproduce. The class doc (`:180`) and the describe (`:15615`) each say two shapes.
